purpose: Brexpiprazole is used to treat schizophrenia and is also used along with an antidepressant to treat major depressive disorder (MDD) when the antidepressant alone is not working well enough. It can also be used to treat agitation related to Alzheimer's dementia. It helps improve mood, thinking, and behavior.
how_it_works: Your brain uses chemical messengers like dopamine and serotonin to regulate mood, thinking, and behavior. In conditions like schizophrenia or depression, these chemicals can be out of balance. Brexpiprazole works by partially activating certain brain receptors and blocking others, helping to bring these chemical signals back into a healthier balance — kind of like a fine-tuning dial rather than an on/off switch.
common_side_effects: Weight gain, feeling sleepy or drowsy, headache, restlessness or an urge to keep moving (akathisia), increased blood sugar, runny nose, and mild tremor. Some people also notice dizziness when standing up too quickly.
warnings: This medication carries a serious warning for elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis — it increases the risk of death and should not be used in that group. It may also increase thoughts of suicide, especially in young adults under 25, particularly when first starting the medication, so it is important to report any changes in mood or behavior right away. Tell your doctor if you have diabetes, high cholesterol, or heart problems, as this medicine can affect blood sugar and cholesterol levels. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: For most adults, the starting dose is 1 mg once daily by mouth. Your doctor may gradually increase this to 2 mg to 4 mg per day depending on how you respond and what condition is being treated. It can be taken with or without food at the same time each day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
